samples: This module reads version strings of the form "major.minor.patch" (for example 1.4.2) into a structured version value, and it reports a specific error when the text has the wrong number of parts or a part is not a non-negative whole number. It can print versions back as dotted text and order them by major, then minor, then patch. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the required one) and a function that picks the highest version from a list, returning nothing for an empty list. It does not handle pre-release or build suffixes, and it has no side effects, so it is safe to use anywhere.

This module reads version numbers written as three dot-separated non-negative whole numbers (major, minor, patch) into a structured value, and prints them back in the same form. It reports a specific error when the text has the wrong number of parts or a part isn't a valid non-negative number. It can also compare versions by major, then minor, then patch, check whether a candidate is compatible with a required version (same major, and not older), and pick the latest version from a list (nothing if the list is empty). It does not handle pre-release or build suffixes, so it suits plain "1.4.2"-style versions only.

This module reads version strings of the form "major.minor.patch" (for example 1.4.2) into a structured version value, and it reports a specific error when the text has the wrong number of parts or a part is not a non-negative whole number. It can print versions back as dotted text and compare them in the usual order (major, then minor, then patch). It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the required one) and a function that picks the greatest version from a list, giving nothing for an empty list. It does not handle pre-release or build suffixes, so use it only for plain three-number versions.

This module reads version strings like "1.4.2" into a structured version value, rejecting text that doesn't have exactly three parts or whose parts aren't non-negative whole numbers (with an error saying which problem occurred). It can print a version back as dotted text, compare versions by major, then minor, then patch, and pick the greatest version from a list (or nothing if the list is empty). It also offers a compatibility check that accepts a candidate only if it has the same major version as the required one and is not older, but it ignores pre-release and build suffixes such as "-beta".

This module reads version strings in the "major.minor.patch" form (for example 1.4.2) into a structured version value, and prints them back the same way. It reports a clear error when the text doesn't have exactly three parts or when a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It also compares versions by major, then minor, then patch, and offers two helpers: one checks whether a candidate is compatible with a required version (same major and not older), and the other picks the highest version from a list, or nothing if the list is empty. It does not support pre-release or build suffixes such as "-beta" or "+build".
